title: What a for loop's header allows

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, where can code use a variable declared in a `for` header, such as `int i = 0`?

options.text: In the rest of the method, once the loop has finished
options.says: The page says the scope of a variable declared in the initialization is limited to the loop.

options.text: In the whole class, as a field that each pass updates
options.says: The page limits the variable's scope to the loop; it never becomes a field.

options.text: In the loop alone, from its first pass to its last
options.says: The page says the scope of variables declared in the initialization is limited to the loop.

questions.stem: Which parts of a basic `for` header does this page say you may leave out?

options.text: Two of them: the initialization and the update
options.says: The page's infinite loop `for (;;)` leaves the condition out as well.

options.text: Three of them: initialization, condition and update
options.says: The page says all three parts are optional, and shows `for (;;)` with none of them.

options.text: One of them: the update that runs after each pass
options.says: The page says the initialization, condition and update parts are all optional.

concepts: A variable declared in the loop's initialization is in scope only inside the loop.
All three parts of the header are optional, and for (;;) is an infinite loop that needs a break.
